text: Most cars have a fuel gauge that shows how much petrol is left. It is there so you can plan a run to the shops without getting stuck. People change small things about their cars all the time. Some swap summer tyres for winter ones. Others ask the car to warm up before a drive on a cold morning. If your back is sore after a long trip, you might say, "Make the seat warmer" or "Tilt the seat back a little." For the tyres, people say, "Check the pressure" or "Put some air in the front ones." To remember where you left the car, you can say, "Save this spot," and later, "Where did I park?"

Divya was a cook, and her feet were tired after a long day. The robot mower in her garden kept stopping halfway across the grass. She said to her phone, "Why does my mower stop?" The assistant checked the mower and said the battery was low. Divya laughed. She would have to practice being patient with it. "Please charge it tonight, and start the weekly mowing again by the end of the week," she said. The assistant told the mower to charge until morning. Then it made a weekly plan for Saturday at nine o'clock. It said the lawn would be cut every Saturday from now on. Divya smiled and went inside to make dinner.

A sports app keeps scores, teams and training plans in one place. It is for knowing how your team is doing without watching every minute. People change a few things all the time. If the score alerts are too noisy, they say, "Mute the alerts for this game." If they want a friend to see the match times, they say, "Share the schedule with Tom." When the battery on a fitness band is low, they ask, "Remind me to charge it." Each match is one item on the list, so you can also say, "Remove that item" or "Move training to Thursday." Simple words are enough.

A sprinkler is for giving the grass water so that it stays green. Most people set it to run early in the morning, when it is cool. You can change how long it runs and on which days. Some people say, "Water the lawn for ten minutes," or "Skip the sprinklers tomorrow, it is going to rain." If the dog digs holes near the fence, you might ask for a little less water there. When neighbours talk about their lawns, they often say, "Turn the sprinklers off for the weekend." A smart controller understands these everyday words and changes the plan for you.

An air purifier cleans the air in a room. It is for people who sneeze a lot, or who live near a busy road. Most purifiers have fan speeds, and people change them often. Say you come home from the market and the room feels stuffy. You might say, "Turn the purifier up," or "Run it faster for an hour." At night people say, "Make it quieter." A plant on the shelf will not clean the air much by itself, so many people keep a purifier too. In a narrow room, one small machine is often enough. To save power, you can say, "Switch it off at eight."

Iris was a busy parent, and the kids were noisy in the back seat. She stopped at a red light and spoke to her phone. "Book a haircut for me on Friday and tell me when the dentist opens." The assistant found a free time at a quarter past four on Friday and booked it. Then it said the dentist opened at eight in the morning. Iris asked it to save the dentist's number, and it did. "Also, put a note in my calendar to call the front desk about Leo's checkup," she said. The assistant added the note. The light turned green, and Iris drove on, glad that she had not needed to look at the screen.

name: tv_off_timer
does: Turns the television off after a set time, and shows a small gold clock on the screen so the warning does not blow past you.
inputs: how long to wait in minutes or hours, and which room; a picnic movie in the garden might need a longer wait
people say:
- Turn the TV off in half an hour
- I'm falling asleep, stop the telly at eleven
- Shut the television down after this film
- Don't let the TV run all night
- Switch off the screen in forty minutes

name: set_volume_limit
does: Sets the highest volume a speaker can reach and a minimum level, so nobody has to listen to something too loud or too quiet.
inputs: which speaker, the highest level from zero to one hundred, and the lowest level
people say:
- Don't let the kitchen speaker get any louder than fifty
- Keep the volume from going too high at night
- The baby is asleep, make the bedroom speaker quieter for good
- Stop it from blasting when I press play
- Never go below twenty, I can't hear it over the dishes

When you buy something online, the shop sends you a tracking number. It is for knowing where your parcel is and when it will come. People change delivery plans often. If you think nobody will be home, you can ask for a different day or a safe place. Some say, "Deliver it to my neighbour," or "Send it to the shop near my work." Delivery windows can be narrow, like between two and four. A new suitcase for a trip might need to arrive before the weekend, so people ask, "Where is my parcel?" or "Can it get here by Friday?" If an order is wrong, they say, "Send it back and give me my money back."

The person wants to send the invitation for a baby shower to everyone on the guest list, even the names at the bottom, from their laptop.
Send the invites
Invite everyone
Email the invitation to the whole list
Can you send the shower invite to all ninety-five guests?
Get the invitations out to everybody, including the last few names
Tell the guests about the party
Please message every person on my guest list about Saturday
I would like the invitation to go to everybody right now, please

name: extend_parking_time
does: Changes the end time of a parking payment, so a long meeting does not end with a ticket, in the main car park or on the street.
inputs: the car or its plate number, and how much longer you need or the new end time
people say:
- I need another hour on my parking
- The meeting is running over, keep the car covered
- Make my parking last until six
- I don't want a fine, can you give me thirty more minutes?
- Pay for more time on the street spot

name: long_trip_battery
does: Gets a phone ready for a long trip, such as a night under the moon or a day with a pack on your back, by turning on extra battery saving like a dimmer screen and fewer updates in the background.
inputs: which phone or tablet, and how many hours it must last
people say:
- My phone is almost dead, make it last
- I'm going hiking all day, save the battery
- Turn on power saving
- Stop my tablet from using so much battery
- I need this phone to survive till tonight

A home alarm is for keeping your house safe when nobody is there. Motion sensors notice movement, and cameras record it. When it gets dark, many cameras switch to night mode. People often forget to turn the alarm on before they leave, so they say, "Arm the alarm when I go out" or "Did I lock up?" Pets can set off sensors, so people say, "Ignore motion in the hallway at night." If a car engine starts in the driveway at a strange hour, you may want to know about it, so you say, "Tell me if the camera sees someone outside."

When you shop in another country, prices are in a different currency. An exchange rate tells you how much your own money is worth there. The rate changes every day, so a price can look cheap on Monday and dear on Friday. People ask, "How much is fifty euros in dollars?" or "What is the rate today?" On a humid holiday in a hot location, nobody wants to do sums by hand. Some phones flash the price in your own money when you point the camera at a sign. You can also say, "Show prices in pounds" to change what you see.

name: keep_dish_warm
does: Keeps a single dish warm in the oven after it is cooked and marks on the display when it will be ready, so food can wait for hours.
inputs: which appliance, how long to keep the dish warm, and a heat level if you want one
people say:
- Keep the lasagne warm until we eat
- Don't let the food go cold, I'll be home at seven
- Hold the oven at low heat for an hour
- Dinner will be late, keep it hot
- Stop cooking but keep it warm

Olivia worked as a cook and had a short nap before her shift. She woke up with a weird thought: her sister's birthday was tomorrow! She grabbed her phone and typed in a hurry, "find a gift for my sister, her birthday is tomorow, under thirty dollars". The assistant showed three ideas. Olivia liked the blue scarf from a shop near her work. "Get that one," she said. The assistant booked a pickup time at the shop for five o'clock and added a reminder to Olivia's calendar. Then it asked if she wanted a card too. Olivia said yes, and she went back to sleep for ten more minutes.

When a pet goes missing on a street, neighbours put up notices and post in the local group. The notice is for finding the animal fast. People change these notices as news comes in. They might say, "Add a new photo," or "Increase the area to the next street." A sharp reminder works well, like "Post it again at six, when people leave work." The notice might also be pinned at the cafe on the corner, and the local group can send an alert. When the pet is found, people say, "Take the post down and say thank you to everyone."

Dmitri was an office worker. He was walking across the big field behind his building when his phone beeped. The storage was almost full. He was about to go on a trip to the west coast and wanted room for photos. "Free up half of my storage," he told the phone. The assistant looked at what was taking up space and said old videos used the most. It offered to move them to the cloud. Dmitri said yes. Next he asked it to pack his ticket and hotel papers into one folder for the trip. The assistant did that too. Now the phone had twice as much free space.

Eilidh was tired after her night shift. In the white light of the car park she whispered to her phone, "How long to get home?" The assistant said the drive was thirty minutes, but traffic on the main road made it ten minutes longer than usual. "Find a faster way," said Eilidh. The assistant showed a route through quiet streets that was five minutes shorter. She also asked it to remind her to switch on the humidifier when she got home, because the flat felt dry. The assistant set a reminder for when she arrived. Eilidh started the car and followed the new route.

Beatriz sat at her desk at work. A delivery van parked outside, and suddenly she remembered that she had left the heater on at home. She spilled a little coffee on her sleeve and rubbed the purple stain with one hand while she typed with the other: "turn off the living room heater and tell me how much power i used todya". The assistant switched off the heater. Then it said she had used eight units so far, which was more than yesterday. It said the heater was the biggest part. Beatriz asked it to remind her to turn the heater down before she left next time.

The person wants to turn on subtitles as a temporary help for a guest who cannot follow the speech.
subtitles on
Put the captions on, please
turn on subtitels
Can we see the words on the screen?
I wear hearing aids but they are out, can you show the text for this show?
My guest has trouble following, could you switch on the subtitles for tonight and turn them off tomorrow?
Show what they are saying
I would like captions for this film

The person wants the speaker to play the morning news while they get ready, hang up the washing and fill the car with fuel.
News
Play the news
Morning news please
Put the news on
I would like to hear the headlines while I get going
Could you read me today's news?
What is going on in the world today?

name: set_water_temperature
does: Sets the water heater to a safe temperature, so the shower is never dangerous, even after a jog when everyone wants a hot wash.
inputs: which water heater, and the temperature in degrees
people say:
- The shower is too hot, turn the water down
- Make the water warmer, I'm cold
- Keep the hot water at a safe level for the kids
- Lower the heater to fifty degrees
- Can you make the water less scalding?

name: suggest_dinner
does: Suggests a dinner for tonight based on what is in the fridge and how the person feels, even after a long nap or a tiring day.
inputs: what food is at home, any diets, and the kind of food wanted, such as light, spicy or a dish from the south
people say:
- What should I cook tonight?
- I have eggs and rice, give me an idea
- Dinner ideas without meat
- I don't know what to eat, help
- Something quick for the kids please

Social media is a place where people post photos and short notes, and see what their friends are doing. Likes show that others enjoyed a post, and followers are people who want to see what you share. Notifications tell you when something happens. There can be too many, so people say, "Mute the alerts at night" or "Only tell me when my sister posts." Say you take a photo of your cereal bowl on a damp Monday morning. You might say, "Post this picture, but only for friends." Later, "Take it down" removes it.

Sara did not like gadgets. Her electricity bill was high, and she did not know why. A neighbour told her to ask the speaker. So Sara said slowly, "Can you tell me how much electricity I use?" The assistant said her house used a constant amount all day, even at night. It measured the fridge, the old freezer in the garage and a charger for her son's electric motorcycle. "The charger is on all night," it said. Sara asked it to switch the charger off every night and turn it on early on Thursday, when her son wanted to ride. The assistant made the plan. Sara smiled and said thank you.

name: world_clock
does: Says what time it is in another city, so a sudden phone call does not wake someone up when their blind is down and the room is dark.
inputs: the name of a city or country (no need to dust off an atlas)
people say:
- What time is it in Tokyo?
- Is it too late to call my brother in Canada?
- Are they awake in Sydney now?
- Time in Lagos
- How many hours ahead is Berlin?

Person: Remind me about my cousin.
Assistant: What should I remind you to do, and when?
Person: Pick her up at the airport. Her plane lands at four, and I want to chill for a while after I close the shop, so remind me one hour before.
Assistant: Done. I will remind you at three to pick up your cousin. Do you want a second reminder?
Person: No, but the roads are usually full on Fridays. Can you make it half an hour earlier?
Assistant: Yes. I will remind you at half past two instead.
Person: Thank you.
Assistant: You are welcome.

A watering timer is for giving plants water when you are busy. It turns the sprinkler on at the same time each day. People change the plan with the weather. In a hot week they may say, "Water the garden twice a day." Before a rainy day, they say, "Skip the next watering." Some systems warn you if the soil is too dry, and you can ask, "Tell me when the tomatoes need water." A small change in time can matter too, so people say, "Move the watering to six in the morning." Seeds need less water than big plants.

name: start_focus_timer
does: Starts a timer for focused work and makes the screen flash when it is time for a break.
inputs: how many minutes to work, how many minutes to rest, and what the break is for, like a crispy snack or a call to your father
people say:
- Let me work for twenty-five minutes, then tell me to stop
- Start a study timer
- I need an hour of quiet work
- Time me, then give me a five minute break
- Keep me on task for half an hour

Fiona did not trust the new thermostat. The screen was small and the buttons were confusing. One cold morning she said to the speaker, "I don't want it hot all day, just warm when I get up." The assistant asked what time that was. "Half past six," said Fiona. It made a schedule: the heating would come on at six, reach twenty degrees by half past, and go down by ten percent during the day. Fiona liked a soft, warm room in the morning, and not a hot one at noon. She thanked the assistant and went back to bed for a few minutes.

Rahul was seven years old and a little afraid of the dark hallway. Before bed he said to the speaker, "Lights on." The hall light came on. "Dimmer," he said, and it became softer. The heater in his room clicked on, and the assistant said the room would be warm soon. Rahul wanted to put his teddy to bed first, so he tucked the bear under the blanket. Then he got in himself and said, "Night light." The assistant turned on the little blue lamp and switched off the hall light. Rahul closed his eyes.

Many homes have a filter that needs changing now and then, like the one in a heater or a cooker hood. A filter is for keeping the air or the water clean and the machine working well. If a pipe leaks or a filter is dirty, you book a repair. People say, "Find a plumber for Tuesday," or "Remind me to change the filter every three months." Some ask for a visit in the middle of the week. Instructions often tell you to fold the old filter before you throw it away. If you have a long list, you can say, "Make a list of repairs for the house."

A restaurant booking holds a table for you at a certain time. It is for avoiding long waits, especially on the weekend. People change bookings often. They say, "Move my table to eight," or "We are five now, not four." If the group is smaller, they reduce the number. Menus show prices, and at the end the total on the bill is what you pay. For takeaway, people ask, "Is the kitchen open?" or "What time do you close?" To cancel, they say, "Cancel my booking."

Anil owned a small shop near an old factory. In the afternoon the sun came through the front window and made the shelves too hot. He spoke to his assistant. "Could you please close the blinds on the window side, because the sun is hurting the chocolates and I do not want them to melt?" The assistant lowered the blinds by half. Anil asked it to reserve that setting for every afternoon, and it saved the plan. The last thing he asked was to open the blinds again at five o'clock. The assistant said that was done.

A birthday reminder is for not forgetting a friend's special day. Phones can sync with your calendar, so dates from your contacts show up every year. People change these things. They say, "Remind me a week before Mum's birthday," so there is time to buy a gift. Gift ideas depend on the person: a card, flowers, or a picnic in the park. If a friend has a sore leg, a quiet dinner may be better than a long walk. You can say, "Find a gift under twenty dollars" or "Add a note to remember what she likes."

Person: Could you please help me with a word, because my son has a Spanish test tomorrow and we are trying to build a short word list over lunch?
Assistant: Happy to help. Which word do you want to translate?
Person: Smooth, like a smooth road.
Assistant: For a road, you say "liso." For things that feel soft, you say "suave." Shall I add "liso" to the list?
Person: Yes please. Can you also tell me what is on his whole test?
Assistant: Sorry, I can't see his school test. But I can quiz him on the list if you like.
Person: That would be great.

Pavel drove a delivery van all day. On his break he looked at his phone, because his grandma was visiting and he wanted dinner to be ready. "Turn the oven on to two hundred degrees and start the fancy coffee machine," he said. The assistant sent both commands to the kitchen at home. Grandma saw the oven light come on and soon smelled coffee. Pavel asked the assistant to make a note: dinner in forty minutes. Then he finished his sandwich and drove on, happy that she would not have to wait.

Francesca woke up with a sudden thought. Was the tax office closed on Fridays? She rubbed her eyes and said, "Could you please tell me when the tax office opens today, and how to get there, because I have to leave some papers before work and I do not want to wait in a long line?" The assistant said it opened at eight and that the walk took twelve minutes. It added the papers to her list. Outside, the snow had started to melt, so the assistant also told her to wear boots. Francesca got up and looked for them.

Tariq was a gardener. While he was trimming the hedge, he cut his hand with the shears. It was not a dangerous cut, but it bled a lot. He took out his phone with the other hand. "Cut hand. Help," he said. The assistant told him to press a clean cloth on the cut and hold his hand up. "Do not touch the cut with dirty hands," it said. After ten minutes the bleeding slowed down. The assistant asked if he wanted to call a doctor. Tariq said no, so it told him how to clean and cover the cut. It also said to skip his evening jog and rest.

On Tuesday, the air in Kai's flat felt dirty. Kai was a grandparent, and the heat from the radiators made the rooms dry and dusty. "Purifier on," Kai said to the speaker. The assistant turned on the purifier in the living room. After a while Kai asked, "Fan faster?" The assistant said it was now on high and the air was getting cleaner. It also offered to turn the purifier down at night so that it would be quiet. Kai said yes, and the assistant set it for ten o'clock.

A packing list is for making sure you bring what you need on a camping trip: a tent, a warm coat, food and a torch. Before leaving, people check the weather in the hills, because it can change fast. They change the list a lot. They say, "Add rain jackets," or "Take off the big tent, we are using the small one." Some families bring a kitten or another pet, so they say, "Put pet food on the list." A trip is more fun with delicious food, so they also say, "Add things for a campfire dinner." If you are not sure how to spell a place name, the assistant can help.

name: get_sports_results
does: Reads out the latest result of a team's match, such as a ball game last night, and says who won; it can connect to a live score feed and has a low-data mode.
inputs: the team name and the sport
people say:
- Did Arsenal win last night?
- What was the score in the cricket?
- How did my team do?
- Any football results from today?
- Who won the basketball game?

Kofi woke up early in a hotel in Lisbon. He expected a quiet morning, but he could hear a car engine outside. His taxi to the airport was coming at seven. "Could you please tell me how to say 'Please take me to the airport' in Portuguese, because it is important and the driver does not speak English?" he asked his phone. The assistant said the sentence slowly and spelled the hard words. Kofi said it back twice. Then he asked the assistant to save the phrase, and it put the phrase on his lock screen. He picked up his bag.

Lei woke up and the room was dim. She grabbed her phone and said, "Could you please check where my parcel is, because it is a toy for my nephew's birthday, and I will be out all day?" The assistant looked up the order and said it was out for delivery, with one stop left before hers. Lei asked it to leave the parcel with the neighbour, and the assistant sent that note to the driver. Then she said, "Please dim the lamp," and the assistant made it softer so she could sleep a few more minutes.

Person: I need to see the dentist.
Assistant: Which day would you like?
Person: Thursday. I am a bit scared of dentists, so please make it a quiet time.
Assistant: I understand. Mornings are usually quieter. Would ten o'clock suit you?
Person: Yes. The bus takes thirteen minutes, so that is fine. Should I bring my own toothbrush?
Assistant: I can't answer for the clinic, but I can add a note to call and ask. Would you like that?
Person: Yes, please.
Assistant: Your visit is booked for Thursday at ten, and the note is added.

The person wants the assistant to check for a water leak, because they were sweeping the kitchen and found a wet floor by a thick pipe.
Any leaks?
Check for a leak
Is water escaping anywhere?
The floor is wet, what is going on with the pipes?
Water is coming into contact with the wall, can you see if something is leaking?
Is the water meter running when nothing is on?
Could you please check the house for leaks, because I will be away for a week and I do not want to come back to a flood?
I think a pipe might be dripping, can you look into it?

The person wants the television sound to stay steady, so the adverts are not louder than the show; the volume is set once and kept flat.
Even out the sound
No loud adverts please
Stop the adverts being so loud
Keep the volume the same all the time
The ads blast my ears, can you do something?
I don't want to run for the remote when I already have my hat and coat on, so please keep the sound even
Turn on the volume leveller
Please make the shows and adverts equally loud, because the baby is asleep next door

Holiday lights are for making a home feel special. Many people use a timer or a light sensor, so the lights come on when it gets dark. The only thing you need to do is plug them in. People change them often. They say, "Turn the tree lights on at five," or "Boost the brightness a bit." For parties, they say, "Play holiday music in the kitchen." Traditions differ from home to home, but plans are easy to change, like "Move dinner to Sunday" or "Remind me to buy gifts on Friday."

Leo was new to the city and had a job interview in the morning. His old alarm clock was broken. After he finished ironing his shirt, he lay down with his head on the pillow and said to his phone, "Alarm six." The assistant set an alarm for six o'clock. "Quiet sound," Leo added, and the assistant picked a soft one. Then it asked if he wanted a second alarm, just in case. Leo said yes, ten minutes later. The assistant set it and said good night.
